maria-support: FYI customer reported p95/p99 spikes and 503s. They noticed GPU OOMs on a few workers around 2026-03-16T16:00Z, impact: slowdowns for tenant 'acme-ux' (dedicated pool).
ryan-runtime: Can you paste the container logs + which model/seq lengths?
sam-cs: Customer says model=rw-13b-8k, typical seq=6k but they ran a few 20k-ish requests yesterday. They say errors coincided with an app rollout.
kelly-sre: Any allocator OOM dumps? nvml output? Even without full OOM, fragmentation + KV growth can push p99 up.
maria-support: Pasted minimal excerpt from one worker log below.

```
[2026-03-16T16:04:59.123Z] WARN runtime: high mem pressure gpu0 used=45.2GB total=48.0GB
[2026-03-16T16:05:02.456Z] ERROR inference: alloc failed: requested=1.2GB available=120MB
[2026-03-16T16:05:02.457Z] ERROR inference: killing request id=req_0x7f9 to free KV cache
[2026-03-16T16:05:03.001Z] INFO tracer: p99 latency jump 2.8s -> 8.9s during reclaim
```
```\n```
ryan-runtime: That looks like KV cache growth + fragmentation. Which runtime flags are set? Any jemalloc/arena config?
alex-sre: Also check if we had an autoscale event or node replacement at that time. KV eviction is async and can stall at p99 if many threads contend.
maria-support: Runtime config is default + dedicated: `kv_cache_enabled=true`, no explicit max_kv_bytes set. Customer on Dedicated so they have large pool.
kelly-sre: Quick mitigation options: 1) set `--max-kv-bytes=32G` 2) enable `--allocator=compact` (one-shot defrag on free) 3) set `--kv-eviction-strategy=aggressive` 4) throttle very long-context requests (server-side request limiter).
ryan-runtime: Agreed. For this customer I'd recommend server-side per-tenant cap: `server.max_context_tokens=8192` and `tenant.rate_limit.long_context=10/min` while we investigate. That avoids a hard restart.
sam-cs: Customer is resistant to full restart but OK with config changes if non-disruptive.
maria-support: I'll request permission to flip those flags and apply via dedicated-config rollout (canary 1/6).
alex-sre: For root cause we need heap and jemalloc stats + nvml sampling during an incident. Steps to collect:
- enable jemalloc stats on the worker: `export MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true,lg_chunk:22` and restart the single worker (drain first)
- start nvml sampling: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu-sample.csv &`
- collect process maps: `pmap -x <pid> > /tmp/pmap.txt`
- gather runtime KV metrics: `curl localhost:9000/metrics | grep kv`

kelly-sre: Also grab `./bin/runtime --pprof-heap` (if compiled with pprof) or `gcore` dump if safe. Avoid multi-gig dumps on prod unless we have space.
ryan-runtime: I've prepared a short reproduction curl that simulates long-context growth — use against a staging worker: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STAGING' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-13b-8k","input":"'$(python -c "print('A'*12000)")'","max_tokens":1}'
```
maria-support: Customer agreed to test throttling on a canary. I'll schedule config rollout at 17:00 PDT.
kelly-sre: After throttling, monitor p95/p99 for 30m. If it drops, we know long-context flight is the main driver. If not, fragmentation/allocator tuning needed.
alex-sre: If we see steady kv_cache_bytes growth without corresponding active sessions, that indicates a leak or retention bug. Check `kv_entries_total` and per-tenant eviction counters.
ryan-runtime: Hotfix plan (short): 1) set `--max-kv-bytes=32G` 2) enable aggressive eviction 3) apply per-tenant context cap 4) canary one worker restart with `allocator=compact`.
sam-cs: Customer accepted hotfix but asked for rollback plan.
maria-support: Rollback plan: revert flags and remove tenant cap; if restart causes regressions, route tenant to backup pool (smaller model) until we resolve.
kelly-sre: Postmortem actions if confirmed: - implement KV soft-limit with backpressure - emit kv_eviction_latency metric - automated per-tenant long-context throttling rule - add allocator defrag window during low traffic
ryan-runtime: I'll open an infra ticket to track changes and attach logs/metrics. deploy-bot: deployment scheduled - canary job started for dedicated-pool-23 (1/6). :rocket:
maria-support: I'll update the customer and ask them to run their long-context repro at 17:10 after canary. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
